title: Atlantic Club recordings in Stockholm
summary: Two albums recorded live at the Atlantic Club, with Peanuts Hucko and a trumpeter she thinks was Billy Butterfield.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, on the same tour with The World's Greatest Jazz Band, you recorded again at the Atlantic Club in Stockholm.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Yes.
And World Jazz Records have put out two albums both recorded on the same night.
Later in October 1975 -- but we don't know the exact date.
We went to -- When we went to Stockholm, it was one of the few places where we had more than a one night stand.
We appeared there for three nights. And then the Atlantic Club got to be a place where we could go each year on an extended engagement. We played two weeks and three weeks at the Atlantic Club.
And, of course, they had -- they brought in apparatus and equipment and recorded right there at the club -- at the Atlantic Club.
So, I did "Wrap Your Troubles In Dreams" and "Just One Of Those Things" for one of the dates.
And then, on the second session I did "I've Got The World On A String" and "Too Marvelous For
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Words."
That last one you haven't recorded before.
No, I haven't recorded that before either.
On two of them, you were accompanied by Peanuts Hucko.
Yeah.

And on the other two, you were accompanied by a trumpet player. And I think we discussed this off tape the last time we were talking. We couldn't remember which one of the two it was. Whether it was Billy Butterfield or Yank Lawson.

You know, I really have to hear the record to tell whether it was Yank or Billy Butterfield. But Billy was with us on one of the -- And it could've been this one, because he was on the first one with us. I mean, at the Atlantic Club.
It's probably Billy.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Well, by analogy, when Bobby Hackett was the guest of the band, he was the trumpet player behind you.
Yes.
So, the question is can we can the same thing about Billy Butterfield?

I'm pretty sure of that, because when these albums were made, The World's Greatest Jazz Band was the extended World's -- They had two of everything. So it's more than likely that it's Billy Butterfield, because Yank would not necessarily accompany me on these things. It was only after the band shot down to the seven pieces that Yank would accompany me. And then, he would not accompany me then either, because he would use either the trombone or the clarinet or reed -- whoever the reed man was. He seldom -- That had to be Billy Butterfield. Yeah.
